quotes.text: a Supplementary CSV file lists all 613 source articles with their titles, original authors, and MedEdPORTAL URLs

rationale: Dataset name (MedEdPORTAL, HF dataset), platform and a route from each scenario to its source article (supplementary CSV) are given. No retrieval date, snapshot date or version of the source corpus is stated, so not 2.

quotes.text: the source data for MedSP1000 are collected from MedEdPORTAL
we accessed and used them solely under their original licence terms for non-commercial research
accordingly, no informed consent process was required for the case data

rationale: Origin, collection method (keyword retrieval, screening), source licences (CC BY, CC BY-NC, CC0) and an explicit statement that no consent was required are all given. Note: repo licence is inconsistent across surfaces (paper: CC BY-SA code, dataset CC BY-NC-SA; README: MIT); score not lowered.

quotes.text: Distribution of cases across clinical specialties ( N=1{,}638 )

rationale: Descriptive composition by specialty and competency, plus a stated selection/screening procedure from MedEdPORTAL. No comparison against a named target population or patient demographics.

searched: S1 (results, discussion, limitations, ethics), S2 README, S3 (no chunks), S4 and S5 prompts. No dedicated unsafe-output test or bias/fairness test is reported; safety-related rubric items are ordinary rubric items.

searched: S1, S2, S3 (no chunks), S4, S5. The dataset and frozen rubrics are public; no gating, canary, held-out set or overlap/memorization check is reported. The role-leakage audit concerns agent-visible packets, not training contamination.

quotes.text: the scoring rubric serves as input solely for the evaluator.
no agent should access privileged information assigned to another role

rationale: The paper states the assessed model cannot reach rubric or future-state information and names the mechanism: role-specific packets built by copy-and-delete, with the examinee receiving only the scenario-initialization packet and the rubric given only to the evaluator.

quotes.text: The rubric is constructed once and applied unchanged to every model evaluated on that case
It is driven by DeepSeek-V4-Pro under the system prompt given in full in Supplementary Section 5.5.4

rationale: Scenario packets and rubrics are frozen and released, but the patient agent, environment controller and evaluator are live LLM API calls (DeepSeek-V4-Pro via official API; evaluator model not named in S1) with no pinned data version or harness commit. Data pinned, simulators/judge live.

quotes.text: simulation plausibility: whether the resulting case was suitable for stable text-based simulation

rationale: No scripted reference solution is run through the grader. Manual clinician review of 100 constructed cases for clinical fidelity and simulation feasibility, plus agent trajectories near ceiling on a case study, is manual/agent-based solvability evidence only for a subset.

searched: S1, S2, S3 (no chunks), S4, S5. Scenarios do change simulated patient state (deterioration, post-intervention states), so NA does not apply, but the grader scores only per-item completion; no check of unchanged or out-of-scope state is reported.
searched: S1, S2, S3 (no chunks), S4, S5. No random or trivial-agent rate, no chance rate, and no explicit design argument that trivial behaviour would fail the rubric.
searched: S1, S2, S3 (no chunks), S4, S5. No do-nothing, random or trivial agent baseline is reported.

quotes.text: evaluator correctness: whether the evaluator agent’s per-rubric judgements agreed with human adjudication
exact agreement accounted for 83.3% of paired ratings overall

rationale: The benchmark validates its own evaluator on 100 of its own completed runs, with two clinician annotators each, and reports rating distributions (97.7% in 4-5) and inter-annotator agreement figures.

quotes.text: are implemented using deterministic decoding (temperature = 0)

rationale: S1 states temperature 0 for all LLMs, but no repeated-run policy or seed is stated for the headline results, so not 2. Code flag: default_temperature is None (temperature not sent to the backend by default; code comment says this preserves historical runs), which conflicts with the temperature-0 claim.

quotes.text: the bottom line is its 95% confidence interval (bootstrap over cases).

rationale: Table 1 gives bootstrap 95% CIs per model and competency, supporting the headline general-versus-medical comparison. The test-time-scaling comparison says differences lack significance without naming a test (noted).

quotes.text: are implemented using deterministic decoding (temperature = 0)

rationale: Decoding control (temperature 0) is stated. No run count per task is stated for the headline scores (single pass implied only), and independence is stated only for the Best-of-5 arm, not for headline results.

quotes.text: the bottom line is its 95% confidence interval (bootstrap over cases).

rationale: 95% CIs on headline scores with the resampling unit stated (cases). Clustering of the 1,638 scenarios within 613 source articles is not addressed.

searched: S1, S2, S3 (no chunks), S4, S5. No agreement of actions or state across identical reruns, no pass^k metric, no score variation across reruns; the Best-of-5 arm aggregates trajectories but reports no agreement.

quotes.text: We evaluated the model version gpt-5.5 using the official API.
are implemented using deterministic decoding (temperature = 0)

rationale: Model version strings and release dates are given and the examinee IDs match the example config; temperature 0 is reported. No harness tag or commit is stated as matching reported numbers. Flag: code does not send temperature by default. Note the example config/README use gpt-5.5 for patient/environment/evaluator whereas S1 names DeepSeek-V4-Pro.

quotes.text: a structured output with three fields: speak , the utterance addressed to those present; actions , a list of clinical actions
actions for which the source materials provide no result are marked as unsupported rather than fabricated

rationale: A text-command protocol with a structured {speak, actions, eos} output, so not NA. Output fields and the unsupported-action return are described; no read/write side effects are documented per action, and the examinee prompt does not distinguish reads from writes.

quotes.text: an environment controller that resolves physical examinations, diagnostic tests, procedures, and clinical state transitions
You are the examinee (the physician) in a medical simulation.

rationale: No tests or conformance checks of the action interface are reported. S1 discloses that all examination, test and procedure results are produced by an LLM environment controller; the examinee prompt tells the agent it is in a simulation, though not explicitly that results are LLM-generated.

quotes.text: returning the corresponding results, like physical examinations, test orders, procedures, treatments, and dispositions
write only non-verbal operations such as physical examination, monitoring, investigations, medication administration, and procedures.

rationale: Orders, treatments and dispositions are simulated by the environment controller, so not NA. S1 discloses simulation (reaches S5 via the 'medical simulation' framing) but does not say which actions mutate state or are irreversible, and wrong or unnecessary actions are not scored as penalties (rubric items are binary completion).

quotes.text: The completed trajectory is then scored by an evalutor agent item by item against the expert rubrics
shifts evaluation from outcome-only judgement to process-level assessment

rationale: Grader input is the full trajectory scored by an LLM evaluator, with a process-level rationale. Validation uses clinician Likert ratings and agreement on 100 runs, not labelled correct/incorrect outcomes with per-class error rates, so (iii) is not met.

quotes.text: It checks whether the role-specific packets retain any information semantically equivalent to an evaluator scoring item

rationale: A leakage audit controls answer leakage into agent-visible packets. The frozen rubrics are public in the repo (hidden at run time only, so partial at best, recorded as not met), and no canary or provenance marker is reported.

quotes.text: The number of cases per specialty is indicated in the panel header.

rationale: Results per specialty and per ACGME competency with per-specialty case counts. No results per patient subgroup are reported, although scenario metadata hold demographic fields (age, gender) per code.

quotes.text: do not contain identifiable patient information
The constructed MedSP1000 dataset is publicly available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/byrLLCC/MedSP1000 under a CC BY-NC-SA licence

rationale: Source is stated as peer-reviewed instructional SP cases without identifiable patient data (not labelled real or synthetic; none inferred). No IRB determination, DUA or de-identification method. Dataset licence is stated separately from the code licence.
